notes.claim: Multiplying complex numbers in rectangular form follows the rules of normal algebra, with j squared put equal to minus one.
Multiplying two complex numbers multiplies their moduli and adds their arguments.
Multiplying by j alone is a pure turn of plus 90 degrees.

sources.title: Complex rotation (video) | Circuit analysis — Khan Academy
sources.quote: Multiplying a real or complex number by the imaginary unit j corresponds to a rotation by +90 degrees.

sources.title: Complex Numbers & Phasors in Polar and Rectangular Form — Electronics Tutorials
sources.quote: The multiplication of complex numbers in the rectangular form follows more or less the same rules as for normal algebra along with some additional rules for the successive multiplication of the j-operator where: j ² = –1.

sources.title: 7_6.dvi — mathcentre
sources.quote: Note that to multiply the two numbers we multiply their moduli and add their arguments.
